newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Reliance cuts polyethylene price.
newsitem.headline: India's Reliance cuts polyethylene price.

text.p: Indian petrochemicals firm Reliance Industries Ltd cut polyethylene price by about 5.0 percent to 47 rupees per kg last week, industry analysts said on Thursday.
They said the move reflected softening global prices and Reliance's strategy to sell higher volumes.
The state-run Indian Petrochemicals Corp Ltd, the other major producer, has not cut its price yet, but might do so any time, analysts said.
January saw Reliance commissioning additional capacities in polypropylene, polyvinyl chloride and polyester filament yarn.
It commissioned a second line of 175,000 tonnes per year of polypropylene at its Hazira works on the western coast, taking its total polypropylene capacity to 350,000 tonnes a year.
Earlier this week, the company announced raising its polyvinyl chloride (PVC) capacity to 270,000 tonnes a year from 180,000 tonnes a year.
